Ulysses.what: Ulysses builds a raft, sails, is wrecked by Neptune and lands on Scheria.
Ulysses weeps at Demodocus' songs and hurls the disc beyond all the Phaeacians.
Ulysses blinds Polyphemus, escapes under the ram and reveals his name.
Ulysses overcomes Circe with Moly and frees his men.
Ulysses passes the Sirens and Scylla and alone survives the ship's wreck.
Ulysses wakes on Ithaca, and Minerva reveals the land and disguises him as a beggar.
Ulysses talks with Penelope in disguise and is recognised by Euryclea by his scar.
Ulysses shoots Antinous and slaughters the suitors, sparing only Phemius and Medon.
Ulysses proves himself to Penelope by describing their immovable bed.
Ulysses reveals himself to Laertes and fights the Ithacans until peace is made.

Jove.what: Jove hears the gods' council and agrees that Ulysses may go home.
Jove sends two fighting eagles as an omen over the Ithacan assembly.
Jove promises the sun-god vengeance and wrecks Ulysses' ship with a thunderbolt.
Jove tells Minerva to make peace in Ithaca with Ulysses ruling.

Minerva.what: Minerva pleads for Ulysses and, as Mentes, urges Telemachus to seek news of his father.
Minerva, as Mentor, readies a ship and crew and sails with Telemachus.
Minerva guides Telemachus at Pylos and flies off as an eagle.
Minerva sends Nausicaa a dream and makes Ulysses look splendid.
Minerva, disguised as a girl, guides the hidden Ulysses to Alcinous' palace.
Minerva reveals Ithaca to Ulysses and disguises him as a beggar.
Minerva, as Mentor and swallow, spurs Ulysses and deflects the suitors' spears.
Minerva halts the fighting and makes a covenant of peace.

Telemachus.what: Telemachus, advised by Mentes, warns the suitors to leave his house.
Telemachus calls the assembly, denounces the suitors and sails secretly for Pylos.
Telemachus asks Nestor for news of Ulysses at Pylos.
Telemachus is recognised by Helen and Menelaus and explains his errand.
Telemachus is reunited with his father Ulysses and plans revenge.
Telemachus nearly strings the bow, then arms himself beside Ulysses.
Telemachus fights beside Ulysses, kills Amphinomus and pleads for Phemius and Medon.

Penelope.what: Penelope despairs at the suitors' plot and is comforted by Minerva's dream.
Penelope talks with the disguised Ulysses, tells of her web and announces the contest.
Penelope brings out Ulysses' bow and proposes the contest of the axes.
Penelope tests Ulysses with the bed and embraces him.

Laertes.what: Laertes is found hoeing, is revealed to by Ulysses, and kills Eupeithes.

Neptune.what: Neptune's anger at Ulysses for blinding Polyphemus is explained to the gods.
Neptune raises a storm and wrecks Ulysses' raft.
Neptune turns the returning Phaeacian ship to stone.

Antinous.what: Antinous blames Penelope's web and tells Telemachus to send her away.
Antinous resolves to ambush Telemachus and lies in wait at Asteris.
Antinous strikes the beggar Ulysses with a footstool.
Antinous scolds the servants and threatens the beggar who asks for the bow.
Antinous is the first suitor killed by Ulysses' arrow.

Eumaeus.what: Eumaeus welcomes the disguised Ulysses but disbelieves he will return.
Eumaeus tells how he was stolen from Syra and sold to Laertes.
Eumaeus leads Ulysses to town and witnesses Melanthius' abuse and Argos.
Eumaeus is shown Ulysses' scar and delivers the bow.
Eumaeus helps Ulysses slaughter the suitors and capture Melanthius.

Euryclea.what: Euryclea packs provisions for Telemachus and swears silence.
Euryclea recognises Ulysses' scar while washing his feet and swears silence.
Euryclea names the twelve guilty maids.
Euryclea tells Penelope that Ulysses is home and the suitors dead.

Eurymachus.what: Eurymachus scorns Halitherses' reading of the eagles and threatens him with a fine.
Eurymachus taunts Ulysses and hurls a stool that hits the cupbearer.
Eurymachus mocks Theoclymenus' warning of doom.
Eurymachus offers compensation, is refused, and is shot by Ulysses.

Agamemnon.what: Agamemnon's ghost tells Ulysses of his murder and warns him against women.
Agamemnon's ghost compares deaths with Achilles and praises Penelope.

Calypso.what: Calypso yields to Jove's decree and helps Ulysses build a raft.

Mercury.what: Mercury delivers Jove's decree to Calypso.
Mercury gives Ulysses the herb Moly against Circe.
Mercury leads the suitors' ghosts down to Hades.

Alcinous.what: Alcinous promises Ulysses an escort and offers him his daughter.
Alcinous calls an assembly, arranges a ship and asks Ulysses his name.
Alcinous sends Ulysses home with gifts and sacrifices after the ship is petrified.

Menelaus.what: Nestor tells Telemachus of the returns and Menelaus' wanderings; Menelaus is mentioned.
Menelaus welcomes Telemachus and tells how he seized Proteus on Pharos.
Menelaus gives Telemachus gifts and farewell.

Medon.what: Medon tells Penelope of the suitors' plot.
Medon is spared by Ulysses at Telemachus' plea.
Medon counsels peace at the Ithacan assembly.

Phemius.what: Phemius is spared by Ulysses at Telemachus' plea.

Philoetius.what: Philoetius laments his master and pledges help to Ulysses.
Philoetius is revealed Ulysses' scar and helps secure the doors.
Philoetius fights beside Ulysses against the suitors.

Circe.what: Circe turns men to pigs, is overcome by Ulysses and restores them.
Circe warns Ulysses of the Sirens, Scylla, Charybdis and the cattle.

Amphinomus.what: Amphinomus urges caution against killing Telemachus.
Ulysses warns Amphinomus to leave before the master returns.

Arete.what: Ulysses supplicates Arete, who recognises the clothes and questions him.

Diana.what: Penelope begs Diana to kill her.

Melanthius.what: Melanthius abuses and kicks the disguised Ulysses at the fountain.
Melanthius brings arms to the suitors, is caught, hung and mutilated.

Mentor.what: Mentor rebukes the Ithacans in the assembly.

Nestor.what: Nestor feasts Telemachus, tells of the Greek returns and sacrifices to Minerva.

Teiresias.what: Teiresias foretells Ulysses' trials, the suitors' killing and a gentle death.

Ajax.what: Ajax's ghost, still angry over the armour, will not speak.

Venus.what: Venus is trapped with Mars in Vulcan's chains in Demodocus' song.

Polyphemus.what: Polyphemus eats Ulysses' men, is blinded, and prays to Neptune to doom him.

Elpenor.what: Elpenor dies falling from Circe's roof.
Elpenor's ghost begs Ulysses for burial.
Elpenor is burned and given a cairn topped with his oar.

Eurylochus.what: Eurylochus escapes Circe's house and reports the men turned to pigs.
Eurylochus persuades the crew to slaughter the sun's cattle.

Halitherses.what: Halitherses reads the eagles as a sign of Ulysses' return and the suitors' doom.

Helen.what: Helen recognises Telemachus, drugs the wine and tells tales of Ulysses at Troy.
Helen reads the eagle and goose omen as Ulysses' coming revenge.

Nausicaa.what: Nausicaa goes to the river, finds Ulysses, clothes him and directs him to town.
Nausicaa bids Ulysses remember her as he leaves.

Pisistratus.what: Pisistratus accompanies Telemachus by chariot from Pylos to Pherae.
Pisistratus and Telemachus are welcomed at Menelaus' palace.

Theoclymenus.what: Theoclymenus, a fugitive seer, joins Telemachus' voyage to Ithaca.
Theoclymenus prophesies that Ulysses is already in Ithaca.
Theoclymenus foretells the suitors' doom and leaves the hall.

Achilles.what: Achilles' ghost says he would rather be a living servant than king of the dead.
Achilles and Agamemnon compare their deaths in Hades.

Amphimedon.what: Amphimedon's ghost tells Agamemnon how the suitors were killed.

Antiphates.what: Antiphates and his Laestrygonians destroy Ulysses' fleet.

Ctesippus.what: Ctesippus throws a heifer's foot at the disguised Ulysses.

Demodocus.what: Demodocus sings of Ulysses and Achilles, Mars and Venus, and the wooden horse.

Dolius.what: Dolius and his sons joyfully greet Ulysses at Laertes' house.

Eurydamas.what: Eurydamas is killed by Ulysses in the battle in the hall.

Hercules.what: Hercules' phantom appears to Ulysses among the dead, fierce and armed.

Laodamas.what: Laodamas boxes at the games and dances with the ball, joining Ulysses' challenge.

Leiodes.what: Leiodes tries and fails to string the bow, warning the suitors of grief.
Leiodes begs for mercy but is killed by Ulysses.

Melantho.what: Melantho taunts Ulysses with Eurymachus in the hall.
Melantho abuses Ulysses and is scolded by Penelope.

Noemon.what: Noemon lends Telemachus a ship for the voyage to Pylos.
Noemon reveals that Telemachus has gone to Pylos, prompting the ambush plot.

Pisander.what: Pisander is killed by the stockman in the battle in the hall.

Polybus.what: Polybus is killed by Eumaeus in the battle in the hall.

Aegyptius.what: Aegyptius opens the assembly, grieving for his son Antiphus.

Aeolus.what: Aeolus gives Ulysses the winds in a sack, then drives him away.

Anticlea.what: Anticlea tells Ulysses of home and her death; he cannot embrace her.

Mars.what: Mars is trapped in chains with Venus by Vulcan in Demodocus' song.

Argos.what: Argos recognises Ulysses after twenty years and dies.

Irus.what: Irus insults Ulysses, fights him and is knocked down and dragged out.

Charybdis.what: Charybdis sucks down the sea; Ulysses escapes it clinging to a fig tree.

Demoptolemus.what: Demoptolemus is killed by Ulysses in the battle in the hall.

Elatus.what: Elatus is killed by Eumaeus in the battle in the hall.

Eupeithes.what: Eupeithes urges the Ithacans to avenge Antinous and leads them against Ulysses; Laertes kills him.

Euryalus.what: Euryalus taunts Ulysses at the games, then apologises with the gift of a sword.

Vulcan.what: Vulcan traps Mars and Venus in chains and exposes them to the laughing gods.

Hyperion.what: Hyperion, told of the slain cattle, threatens Jove, who promises to wreck the ship.

Idothea.what: Idothea helps Menelaus seize Proteus, who reveals the fates of Ajax, Agamemnon and Ulysses.

Ino.what: Ino gives Ulysses her veil as Neptune wrecks his raft.

Laestrygonians.what: The Laestrygonians kill the crews and sink all of Ulysses' ships but his own.

Lampetie.what: Lampetie tells her father the sun-god that Ulysses' men have killed the cattle.

Leiocritus.what: Leiocritus dismisses Telemachus' request for a ship, and the assembly breaks up.

Mentes.what: Minerva as Mentes urges Telemachus to call an assembly and seek news at Pylos.

Proteus.what: Seized by Menelaus on Pharos, Proteus reveals the fates of Ajax, Agamemnon and Ulysses.

Scylla.what: Scylla seizes six of Ulysses' men from the ship as it passes her cave.

Sirens.what: The Sirens sing to lure Ulysses' ship, but he passes bound to the mast.
